title: Extension of a stable generic pointed curve
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $S$ an integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme with generic point $\eta$ and function field $K$. Let $C_\eta$ be a smooth projective geometrically integral $K$-curve of genus at least two, with distinct $K$-rational points $p_1,\ldots,p_n$, where $n$ may be zero. There are an integral scheme $T$ of finite type over $S$, an alteration $r:T\to S$ with finite separable function-field extension, and a stable pointed curve $(W\to T,s_1,\ldots,s_n)$ whose generic pointed fibre is identified with $(C_\eta,p_1,\ldots,p_n)\times_K k(T)$. Projectivity of $W\to T$ may initially be in the projective-bundle sense: a closed immersion into the projective bundle of a finite-type quasi-coherent module [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. No morphism from $W$ to another specified $S$-curve and no group action on $W$ is asserted. The stable pointed conditions are preserved by arbitrary base change.

A stable pointed curve over a scheme $T$ means a projective flat finitely presented family with nonempty connected reduced geometric fibres of pure dimension one, whose only singularities are ordinary double points, together with finitely many disjoint sections in its relative smooth locus. On the normalization of each irreducible component of every geometric fibre, a component of genus zero has at least three special points and one of genus one has at least one; special points are inverse images of nodes or markings. An ordinary double point has completed geometric local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. The marking may be empty. A genus is computed on the smooth projective normalization of a geometric component. The markings are unordered when isomorphisms are allowed to permute them.

The notions of field, integral scheme, proper morphism, finite type, geometric integrality, dimension, projectivity, finite morphism, surjectivity, function field and field extension use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension] and [def-pc-field-tower]. H-projective means admitting a closed immersion into some finite-dimensional projective space over the target. Normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. An alteration is a proper surjective morphism of integral schemes that is finite over a dense open of its target. Group actions may be nonfaithful and may act on the ground field. Flatness, finite presentation, smoothness, geometric fibres, closed immersions, fibre products and etaleness use [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-pc-fibre-product] and [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Normalization, completion and power series use [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]; the genus of a smooth projective geometrically integral curve is [def-pc-genus].

proof.text: Put $g=g(C_\eta)\geq2$. Apply [lem-sfb-projective-stable-pointed-level-parameter] with $(k,g,n)$; clause (b) with $F=K$ supplies the nonempty finite etale $K$-scheme $P_{C_\eta}$ representing labelled pairs $(m_\eta,\alpha_\eta)$. The projective structure morphism of $S$ is proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper], hence separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus the integral finite-type $S$ meets the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-finite-etale-generic-normal-cover]; apply it to $S$ and $P_{C_\eta}$. Obtain $L/K$ finite separable, $u:\operatorname{Spec}L\to P_{C_\eta}$ and its finite normal cover $q:S_L\to S$ with specified generic fibre and field $L$. The representing bijection evaluated on $u$ gives $m_\eta:\operatorname{Spec}L\to M$ and the actual labelled isomorphism $\alpha_\eta:(\mathcal U_{m_\eta},t_i)\simeq(C_\eta,p_i)_L$.

source.place: Lemma 3.7, printed p.608, expanded using de Jong (1996), Sections 2.24 and 4.17.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-projective-generic-map-graph-alteration] with $N=S_L$, its specified generic map $j_L$, the projective finite-type parameter scheme $M$ and $a=m_\eta$. Step 1 gives $q$ finite and surjective, $S_L$ normal integral of finite type over $k$, and $j_L$ identifying both the function field and the generic fibre with $L$; these are exactly its hypotheses on $N$ and $q$. Its reduced graph closure gives integral $T$, the alteration $r:T\to S$ of finite type, and $m:T\to M$ with $k(T)=L$ as a $K$-extension induced by $r$ and $m|_{\operatorname{Spec}L}=m_\eta$. Thus the alteration has precisely the finite separable extension chosen above.

source.place: Lemma 3.7, printed p.608, expanded using de Jong (1996), Sections 2.24 and 4.17.

proof.text: Set $(W,s_i)=(\mathcal U,t_i)\times_M T$. By clause (a) of [lem-sfb-projective-stable-pointed-level-parameter], this is a stable pointed curve with the permitted projective-bundle projectivity. The universal property in [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies its generic fibre with $(\mathcal U_{m_\eta},t_i)$ because $m\circ j_T=m_\eta$; composing with $\alpha_\eta$ identifies it with $(C_\eta,p_i)_L$, preserving every label. For any $T'\to T$, both iterated pullback and $(\mathcal U,t_i)\times_M T'$ have the same universal property, with the same projections and sections. Clause (a) applies to the composite $T'\to M$ and gives all stable conditions without restrictions on $T'$, including nonreduced, non-Noetherian, disconnected and empty bases. Forgetting labels yields the unordered marking convention.
